title: Getting the confession
situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android from the attic sits handcuffed across the table, trembling, covered in his owner's dried blood. He has not said a word to {{Hank}} and the other detectives. You can see his stress level rising. You know that androids under extreme stress can self-destruct. You could connect to him directly and force the memory out, which would almost certainly push him over the edge.

options.text: Talk him through it calmly and build enough trust that he confesses.
Pressure him hard with the evidence to crack him quickly.
Grab his arm and probe his memory by force.
Stop the interrogation without a confession.

outcomes.0: Slowly, the android begins to talk. He says his owner beat him every day and that he killed him because he was afraid; he wrote the words on the wall because something told him to. {{Hank}} and the detectives have their confession.
outcomes.1: Under pressure the android breaks and confesses, shaking: his owner beat him every day and he killed him because he was afraid. His stress is dangerously high.

title: When the officer grabs him
situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android has confessed and said he killed because his owner beat him every day. As officers move to take him back to his cell he panics; one detective grabs him roughly and the android starts screaming for them not to touch him. His stress is spiking. You could insist they stop and let him walk himself, or stand back and let the police handle their prisoner.

options.text: Step in and tell the officers to stop handling him.
Stand back and let the police do their job.

adaptationNote: After a calm confession, intervening gets him safely back to his cell. After a pressured confession, intervening lets him grab an officer's gun, shoot you, and shoot himself. Standing back leads to his suicide either way.
